label: About
title: About The Rows That Fade Into Paper
short_blurb: A daily generated front page where the image is the interface.
body: Daily Frontpage is a daily generated interactive front page. Each edition starts from a saved source, becomes a new image-led scene, and stays explorable in the archive. The image is the interface: a visible mark in the scene opens the real source that shaped the day.

This edition began with one saved post, @yoheinakajima: if you're interested in simulation games, you'll like this research i worked.... Its image from pbs.twimg.com set the palette, contrast, edge behavior, and gesture. The scene became The Rows That Fade Into Paper: A flat orthographic print plate of cool grey paper holding horizontal bands of tiny one-bit dithered pictograms: pylon, pyramid, roof, pause circle, flag on hill. The bands are arranged as a descending stepped terrace across a wide landscape canvas. After the image was made, a plate-reading pass mapped the source to Ragged stepped edge where dithered glyph bands dissolve into paper.

typography.rationale: Fraunces and Newsreader fit image-led art objects while Space Grotesk keeps process labels crisp.
